hypotheses.claim: On dev_24 with a 2000 ms budget, the current LNS skeleton is empirically saturated near mean objective 16.05 (SBS 16.0496 across 7 archived solvers, VBS gap only 0.82%), meaning gains must come from per-iteration diversification rather than more iterations. I therefore claim that replacing a static multiplicative-gate rank-power ruin score with a stagnation-adaptive exponent plus capacity-slack-aware gating will reduce mean objective by >= 0.02 (i.e. below 16.030) on cvrp_dev_hetero_24, with the largest gains concentrated in the 'tight' capacity and 'clustered' spatial regimes where the VBS relative gap is most negative (-22.7% and -19.6%).

next_search_advice.direction: Evolution of the multiplicative gate + rank-power ruin priority rule score_i = rank_power(|removal_savings_i|/scale * gate_load * gate_depot * gate_demand * gate_rdist, p(iter_frac, stagnation_ratio)), tuned toward the weakest regimes of dev_24 (tight capacity, uniform demand, n=100, eccentric depot): strengthen gate_load with a fill-ratio term (route_load/capacity) so near-full routes are ruptured first, add a dimensionless demand-over-slack term (demands_i/(capacity - route_load + demands_i)) to target customers whose removal frees scarce slack on tight instances, and make the rank exponent p monotone increasing in stagnation_ratio so early iterations exploit high absolute savings while stagnating iterations flatten the ranking toward diversification. Keep deterministic tie-breaking (index order) and all state arrays read-only.
